The **Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge** (simplified Chinese:丹昆特大桥; traditional Chinese:丹昆特大橋; pinyin:_Dān-Kūn tèdà qiáo_) is a 164.8-kilometre-long (102.4 mi)viaduct on the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-Buckley-2) It is the longest bridge in the world since its designation by Guinness World Record in 2011.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-Guinness-3)
Map of the bridge

The bridge is located on the rail line between Shanghai and Nanjing in Jiangsu province. It is in the Yangtze River Delta, where the geography is characterized by lowland rice paddies, canals, rivers, and lakes. The bridge runs roughly parallel to the Yangtze River, about 8 to 80 km (5 to 50 mi) south of the river. It passes through the northern edges of population centers (from west to east) beginning in Danyang, Changzhou, Wuxi, Suzhou, and ending in Kunshan. There is a 9-kilometre-long (5.6 mi) section over open water across Yangcheng Lake in Suzhou.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-Farooq-1)
Construction was completed in 2010 and the bridge opened in 2011. Employing 10,000 people, the project took four years and cost about $8.5 billion.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-Farooq-1) The bridge currently holds the Guinness World Record for the longest bridge in the world in any category as of June 2011.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-Guinness-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-4)
The China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC), a subsidiary of China Communications Construction Company designed and built the bridge. It is a Chinese government-funded company which was originally part of the Foreign Aid Office of the Ministry of Communications of China. This company leads major civil engineering projects in China like highways, railways, bridges, ports, and tunnels.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-5)

The world's longest bridge is the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge in China, part of the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway, according to Encyclopaedia Britannica. The bridge, which opened in June 2011, spans 102.4 miles (165 kilometers).
China constructed the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge in just four years, employing 10,000 workers, at a cost of about $8.5 million, according to Encyclopaedia Britannica. It crosses low rice paddies, part of the Yangtze River Delta, with just a few miles of the bridge actually crossing the open water of Yangcheng Lake in Suzhou. The bridge averages about 100 feet (31 meters) off the ground.

The majority of Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge's length follows the Yangtze River, at a distance varying between 5 and 50 miles (8 and 80 kilometers) south of it. The section that crosses Yangcheng Lake in Suzhou is 5.6 miles (9 kilometers) long and is supported by 2,000 pillars, Engineering Clicks reported.

# What's the world's longest bridge?
### What is the second longest bridge?
The second longest bridge in the world is the Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct in Taiwan, according to BBC Science Focus. This 97.8 mile (157.3 kilometer) bridge was built in 2007 to resist seismic activity during earthquakes, according to Encyclopaedia Britannica.

A viaduct is a specific type of long bridge, usually consisting of a series of arches or columns. The bridge is part of the Taiwan High Speed Rail and stretches from Zuoying in Kaohsiung and Baguashan in Chang-hua County.

# What's the world's longest bridge?
### Other notable bridges
The world's longest road bridge is the 34-mile (55-km) long Bang Na expressway in Thailand, which was constructed in 2000, according to Guinness World Records. This road bridge is a six-lane elevated highway that crosses only a bit of water, the Bang Pakong River.

Upon construction of the massive bridge, the Bang Na temporarily became the longest bridge in the world, according to the database Transport Research International Documentation (TRID). This database documents the total area of the bridge's surface at 20,400,000 square feet (1,900,000 square meters).
The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is the world's longest continuous bridge over water.
(Image credit: Gary Fowler/Shutterstock)
The world's longest continuous bridge over water is the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway in southern Louisiana. The causeway is actually two parallel bridges, with the longer of the two measuring close to 24 miles (39 km), according to Encyclopaedia Britannica. The bridges are supported by 9,500 concrete pilings, according to the American Concrete Institute.
Louisiana's famous bridge faced a challenger in 2011, when China claimed that its Jiaozhou Bay Bridge was the longest spanning water. Guinness World Records decided to split the title into two parts, stating that the 26.4-mile (42.5-km) long Jiaozhou Bay Bridge is the longest bridge over water in aggregate, while the Pontchartrain is the longest continuous bridge, according to World Atlas. In Jiaozhou, land bridges and sea tunnels make up parts of the overall structure.

Ask most people to name the world’s longest bridge, and you’re likely to get a confident answer like the Golden Gate Bridge or the Brooklyn Bridge or some other famous landmark plastered across postcards and movies. But the world’s longest bridge is not a tourist attraction or an architectural icon in the traditional sense. It is the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge, a 164.8-kilometre engineering marvel on China’s Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railroad.
Day after day, trains carrying commuters, students, and business travellers glide across its length, crossing wetlands, fish farms, rivers, canals, and endless paddy fields. Most passengers never realise they are travelling over a structure that holds a world record.
Its quiet existence is part of what makes it remarkable. Unlike bridges celebrated for dramatic skylines or dizzying heights, the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge, known as the longest bridge in the world**,** was built for efficiency, speed, and scale. It is a testament to modern engineering on a level so vast that it often goes unnoticed, a record-breaking structure hiding in plain sight, carrying people across one of the busiest rail corridors on Earth.

## World Records
**Record****Bridge****Country**  
Longest Bridge in the World Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge China  
Biggest or the Largest Bridge in the World Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge China  
Highest Bridge in the World Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge China  
Tallest Bridge in the World Millau Viaduct France
These four titles get mixed up constantly, and each one describes a different kind of record. Keep reading since every one of them is explained below.
Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge is the longest bridge in the world. Running 164.8 kilometres through Jiangsu Province, the Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge (also written Danyang–Kunshan) carries the Beijing –Shanghai High-Speed Railway from the coast into the country’s interior. Construction began in 2006 and finished in 2010, at a cost of roughly US$8.5 billion, with the line opening to passengers the following year.
Rather than crossing a single river or valley, the bridge threads through cities, lakes, rice paddies and wetlands on more than 9,500 concrete piers, allowing bullet trains to hold speeds of up to 300 km/h without slowing for the ground below.
For travellers, this is precisely what makes it worth experiencing: a window seat on the Beijing – Shanghai line offers an uninterrupted view over the Yangtze Delta countryside for nearly two hours, covering scenery that would otherwise take a full day to see by road. The bridge has held its Guinness World Record since 2011, and no other structure has come close to challenging it since.

## Can You Visit the World’s Longest Bridge?
Yes, and the simplest way is to book a seat on the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway journey through China. Any train running this route crosses the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge as a matter of course, so no special ticket or detour is required; a window seat on the Nanjing–Suzhou stretch is enough to appreciate its scale.
As the bridge is elevated and built for 300 km/h running, there is no pedestrian access or dedicated viewing platform along most of its length. The experience is meant to be had from inside the train, watching wetlands and rice fields drift by beneath you.

## Fascinating Facts About the Longest Bridge in the World
1.   It took roughly four years to build, from 2006 to 2010, at a cost of about US$8.5 billion.  
2.   More than 9,500 concrete piers support the structure across its full 164.8 km length.  
3.   It crosses rivers, canals, lakes and wetlands without a single road or rail crossing at ground level.  
4.   It carries Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway trains at speeds of up to 300 km/h.  
5.   It has held the Guinness World Record for the longest bridge since 2011, with no serious challenger in sight.

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
Length alone doesn’t tell you much unless you know what each bridge actually carries, why it was built that long, and what makes it worth knowing about. Here’s the full list.
**SR No.****Bridge****Country****Length****Bridge Type**  
1 Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge China 164.8 km Railway viaduct  
2 Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct Taiwan 157.3 km High-speed rail viaduct  
3 Tianjin Grand Bridge China 113.7 km Railway bridge  
4 Cangde Grand Bridge China 105.8 km Railway bridge  
5 Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge China 79.7 km Railway bridge  
6 Bang Na Expressway Thailand 54 km Elevated highway  
7 Beijing Grand Bridge China 48.15 km Railway viaduct  
8 Dhaka Elevated Expressway Bangladesh 46.7 km Elevated expressway  
9 Metro Manila Skyway System Philippines 39.2 km Elevated expressway  
10 Lake Pontchartrain Causeway USA 38.42 km Road bridge

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 1. Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge: China – 164.8 km
The reigning record-holder since 2011, this elevated viaduct carries the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway across Jiangsu’s lakes, wetlands, and rice paddies on more than 9,500 concrete piers. Trains cross at up to 300 km/h without a single ground-level obstruction. For travellers, it’s the rare record you can experience simply by booking a train ticket rather than a special tour.

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 2. Changhua – Kaohsiung Viaduct: Taiwan – 157.3 km
The Changhua–Kaohsiung Viaduct in Taiwan was engineered so that bullet trains could stop safely mid-span during an earthquake, a genuine priority in one of the world’s most seismically active regions. It crosses flood-prone farmland and urban corridors, keeping western Taiwan connected at full speed year-round.

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 3. Tianjin Grand Bridge: China – 113.7 km
The Tianjin Grand Bridge, another segment of the Beijing–Shanghai line, runs between Langfang and Qingxian using modular precast sections that considerably sped up construction. It allows trains to bypass rivers, roads and flood zones north of Tianjin, keeping the capital-to-Shanghai run smooth and largely invisible to the passengers riding it.

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 4. Cangde Grand Bridge: China – 105.8 km
The Cangde Grand Bridge crosses the Wei River on more than 3,000 seismic-resistant piers, forming another critical link along the world’s busiest high-speed rail corridor. It is less well known than its record-holding neighbours, but structurally, it is among the most heavily reinforced sections of the entire route.

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 5. Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge: China – 79.7 km
The Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge, part of the Zhengzhou–Xi’an High-Speed Railway, briefly held the title of the world’s longest bridge before the Beijing–Shanghai corridor overtook it. It spans the Wei River, a major tributary of the Yellow River, using continuous beam and box-girder construction to keep central China’s rail network running at speed.

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 6. Bang Na Expressway: Thailand – 54 km
The Bang Na Expressway in Thailand is the longest bridge built for road vehicles anywhere in the world. This elevated Bangkok tollway floats above existing streets rather than crossing water, built with 1.8 million cubic metres of concrete to ease congestion across Metro Bangkok without touching a river, sea or valley.

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 7. Beijing Grand Bridge: China – 48 km
The Beijing Grand Bridge guides bullet trains through the capital’s outskirts, bypassing dense road traffic and shifting terrain. Built with prefabricated box girders for faster assembly, it forms the final high-speed link between Beijing and the wider Beijing–Shanghai corridor.

##### **_John William Strutt, 3rd Baron Rayleigh died_**
John William Strutt, 3rd Baron Rayleigh was a British mathematician and physicist who made extensive contributions to science. He spent all of his academic career at the University of Cambridge. Among many honours, he received the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physics "for his investigations of the densities of the most important gases and for his discovery of argon in connection with these studies." Reading Time:  8 minutes
Ask most people to name the world’s longest bridge, and you’re likely to get a confident answer like the Golden Gate Bridge or the Brooklyn Bridge or some other famous landmark plastered across postcards and movies. But the world’s longest bridge is not a tourist attraction or an architectural icon in the traditional sense. It is the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge, a 164.8-kilometre engineering marvel on China’s Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railroad.
Day after day, trains carrying commuters, students, and business travellers glide across its length, crossing wetlands, fish farms, rivers, canals, and endless paddy fields. Most passengers never realise they are travelling over a structure that holds a world record.
Its quiet existence is part of what makes it remarkable. Unlike bridges celebrated for dramatic skylines or dizzying heights, the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge, known as the longest bridge in the world**,** was built for efficiency, speed, and scale. It is a testament to modern engineering on a level so vast that it often goes unnoticed, a record-breaking structure hiding in plain sight, carrying people across one of the busiest rail corridors on Earth.

These four titles get mixed up constantly, and each one describes a different kind of record. Keep reading since every one of them is explained below.
Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge is the longest bridge in the world. Running 164.8 kilometres through Jiangsu Province, the Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge (also written Danyang–Kunshan) carries the Beijing –Shanghai High-Speed Railway from the coast into the country’s interior. Construction began in 2006 and finished in 2010, at a cost of roughly US$8.5 billion, with the line opening to passengers the following year.
Rather than crossing a single river or valley, the bridge threads through cities, lakes, rice paddies and wetlands on more than 9,500 concrete piers, allowing bullet trains to hold speeds of up to 300 km/h without slowing for the ground below.
For travellers, this is precisely what makes it worth experiencing: a window seat on the Beijing – Shanghai line offers an uninterrupted view over the Yangtze Delta countryside for nearly two hours, covering scenery that would otherwise take a full day to see by road. The bridge has held its Guinness World Record since 2011, and no other structure has come close to challenging it since.
texts.2:
## Can You Visit the World’s Longest Bridge?
Yes, and the simplest way is to book a seat on the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway journey through China. Any train running this route crosses the Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge as a matter of course, so no special ticket or detour is required; a window seat on the Nanjing–Suzhou stretch is enough to appreciate its scale.
As the bridge is elevated and built for 300 km/h running, there is no pedestrian access or dedicated viewing platform along most of its length. The experience is meant to be had from inside the train, watching wetlands and rice fields drift by beneath you.
texts.3:
## Fascinating Facts About the Longest Bridge in the World
1.   It took roughly four years to build, from 2006 to 2010, at a cost of about US$8.5 billion.  
2.   More than 9,500 concrete piers support the structure across its full 164.8 km length.  
3.   It crosses rivers, canals, lakes and wetlands without a single road or rail crossing at ground level.  
4.   It carries Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway trains at speeds of up to 300 km/h.  
5.   It has held the Guinness World Record for the longest bridge since 2011, with no serious challenger in sight.

## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 1. Danyang Kunshan Grand Bridge: China – 164.8 km
The reigning record-holder since 2011, this elevated viaduct carries the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway across Jiangsu’s lakes, wetlands, and rice paddies on more than 9,500 concrete piers. Trains cross at up to 300 km/h without a single ground-level obstruction. For travellers, it’s the rare record you can experience simply by booking a train ticket rather than a special tour.
texts.7:
## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 2. Changhua – Kaohsiung Viaduct: Taiwan – 157.3 km
The Changhua–Kaohsiung Viaduct in Taiwan was engineered so that bullet trains could stop safely mid-span during an earthquake, a genuine priority in one of the world’s most seismically active regions. It crosses flood-prone farmland and urban corridors, keeping western Taiwan connected at full speed year-round.
texts.8:
## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 3. Tianjin Grand Bridge: China – 113.7 km
The Tianjin Grand Bridge, another segment of the Beijing–Shanghai line, runs between Langfang and Qingxian using modular precast sections that considerably sped up construction. It allows trains to bypass rivers, roads and flood zones north of Tianjin, keeping the capital-to-Shanghai run smooth and largely invisible to the passengers riding it.
texts.9:
## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 4. Cangde Grand Bridge: China – 105.8 km
The Cangde Grand Bridge crosses the Wei River on more than 3,000 seismic-resistant piers, forming another critical link along the world’s busiest high-speed rail corridor. It is less well known than its record-holding neighbours, but structurally, it is among the most heavily reinforced sections of the entire route.
texts.10:
## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 5. Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge: China – 79.7 km
The Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge, part of the Zhengzhou–Xi’an High-Speed Railway, briefly held the title of the world’s longest bridge before the Beijing–Shanghai corridor overtook it. It spans the Wei River, a major tributary of the Yellow River, using continuous beam and box-girder construction to keep central China’s rail network running at speed.
texts.11:
## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 6. Bang Na Expressway: Thailand – 54 km
The Bang Na Expressway in Thailand is the longest bridge built for road vehicles anywhere in the world. This elevated Bangkok tollway floats above existing streets rather than crossing water, built with 1.8 million cubic metres of concrete to ease congestion across Metro Bangkok without touching a river, sea or valley.
texts.12:
## Top 10 Longest Bridges in the World
### 7. Beijing Grand Bridge: China – 48 km
The Beijing Grand Bridge guides bullet trains through the capital’s outskirts, bypassing dense road traffic and shifting terrain. Built with prefabricated box girders for faster assembly, it forms the final high-speed link between Beijing and the wider Beijing–Shanghai corridor.

texts.1:
The bridge is located on the rail line between Shanghai and Nanjing in Jiangsu province. It is in the Yangtze River Delta, where the geography is characterized by lowland rice paddies, canals, rivers, and lakes. The bridge runs roughly parallel to the Yangtze River, about 8 to 80 km (5 to 50 mi) south of the river. It passes through the northern edges of population centers (from west to east) beginning in Danyang, Changzhou, Wuxi, Suzhou, and ending in Kunshan. There is a 9-kilometre-long (5.6 mi) section over open water across Yangcheng Lake in Suzhou.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-Farooq-1)
Construction was completed in 2010 and the bridge opened in 2011. Employing 10,000 people, the project took four years and cost about $8.5 billion.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-Farooq-1) The bridge currently holds the Guinness World Record for the longest bridge in the world in any category as of June 2011.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-Guinness-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-4)
The China Road and Bridge Corporation (CRBC), a subsidiary of China Communications Construction Company designed and built the bridge. It is a Chinese government-funded company which was originally part of the Foreign Aid Office of the Ministry of Communications of China. This company leads major civil engineering projects in China like highways, railways, bridges, ports, and tunnels.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danyang%E2%80%93Kunshan_Grand_Bridge#cite_note-5)
